newsitem.title: CONGO: Congo breaks with Polisario's Sahara Republic.
newsitem.headline: Congo breaks with Polisario's Sahara Republic.

text.p: The Central African state of Congo has broken diplomatic ties with the Polisario Front's self-proclaimed republic in the Western Sahara, pending a delayed U.N. referendum on the disputed territory's future.

"There can be no independent entity on this territory before organisation of the referendum envisaged by the international community and accepted by the concerned parties," government spokeswoman Sophie Moukouyou told reporters on Thursday.

A U.N.-organised referendum was to have been held in 1992 to decide whether Western Sahara, a former Spanish colony, should be incorporated into Morocco, which controls most of the territory, or become independent, as sought by Polisario.

Oil producer Congo recognised Polisario's Saharan Arab Democratic Republic in the 1980s. Officials say Congo's new prime minister, Charles David Ganao, is due to make a three-day official visit to Morocco on September 17.
A U.N.-monitored ceasefire has been in effect since 1991 but the referendum has been repeatedly postponed because of differences over who should be allowed to vote.
A recent report by U.N. Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali said it was unlikely the voter identification process would be resumed any time soon.
